channel.title: IndieHOT — Indie Game Hot Topics
channel.description: IndieHOT collects indie game news from a set of public sources every day and scores it by rules: engines & tools, publishing & marketing, devlogs, industry & funding, events, reviews & postmortems. Only titles, one-line self-written summaries and outbound links are shown — no full text is republished.

item.title: Why Your Game VO Always Sounds "Off" — And It's Not the Actors
item.description: Uneven game voiceover is usually a loudness problem, not a performance one — the piece explains how aligning every line to the same LUFS and true-peak targets fixes it.

item.title: Expanding Anyma’s Coachella performance into broadcast AR with Unreal Engine
item.description: Anyma's Coachella show used Unreal Engine, MetaHuman and broadcast AR to bring its live-music visuals to a wide online audience.

item.title: Are the new wave of solo AI game-makers making any money? No, not really
item.description: Games built with AI tools like Claude Code are flooding the app stores, but very few are earning meaningful revenue or downloads — a sober look at solo AI game-making.

item.title: China's Game Market Revenue Hit 30 Billion Yuan in October, Down 4.27% YoY: Mobile Down 2.2%, PC Down 15%
item.description: Gamma Data reports China's game market revenue reached 30 billion yuan in October, down 4.27% year over year, with mobile down 2.2% and PC down 15%.

item.title: This Unity Fluid Simulation Tool Lets You Add Realistic Wet Lens Effects
item.description: Fluid Frenzy 2.0 lets Unity developers add realistic rain and wet-lens effects to their in-game cameras, and this article walks through what is new.

item.title: Appcharge launches Checkout Experimentation Lab for D2C sales
item.description: Payments platform Appcharge launched a Checkout Experimentation Lab that lets publishers A/B test their direct-to-consumer checkout pages to tailor the final step of payment for each player.

item.title: Data digest: Pixel Flow, Monster Hunter, October’s top games, Nintendo numbers, more
item.description: This week's mobile data digest covers Pixel Flow, Monster Hunter, October's top games and Nintendo's numbers, plus business updates from Liftoff and other publishers.

item.title: Stylized Roguelite Developer Shares Three Unusual Game Optimization Tricks
item.description: The developers of Barrow and Blade share three unconventional tricks for squeezing performance out of their stylized roguelite.

item.title: Best animation library for Unity UI Toolkit: Cascade vs PrimeTween vs LitMotion
item.description: All three libraries can fade and move UI elements, but they were built for different jobs; the author tested them side by side in one Unity 6000.4 project to guide the choice.

item.title: Unity acquires Synty Studios to bring its asset library to Unity Spark
item.description: Unity has acquired Synty Studios, maker of the Polygon range of stylised 3D packs, bringing more than 60,000 low-poly assets into its AI-native creation platform Unity Spark.

item.title: Pixel Art for a Game Jam: My 16x16 Coin Sprite Sheet Workflow
item.description: The author turns a two-hour struggle with one spinning coin at a game jam into a complete workflow for a 16x16, four-frame coin sprite sheet that plays crisply in Phaser.

item.title: What the first 60 seconds of two idle browser games taught us (with real numbers)
item.description: Real numbers from two tiny 1.6 MB JavaScript idle games break down what keeps players past the first 60 seconds — practical data for web idle-game devs.

item.title: Unreal Insights in the Sprint: A Short Performance Pass You Can Finish Before Standup
item.description: A quick Unreal Insights performance pass you can finish before standup, turning profiling into a routine instead of a fire drill.

item.title: Hand Tracking vs Controllers in VR: How to Choose
item.description: Choose controllers when a VR game needs precision, buttons and haptic feedback, and hand tracking when ease of use matters more, such as training, casual play and public demos.

item.title: Designing a browser game older players can start in ten seconds: what the classics get right
item.description: Classic card, board and puzzle games need no tutorial, never punish slow reactions and allow undoing a mistake — design choices any browser game can borrow.

item.title: Wild Shift Devlog #6: I couldn't find my own @
item.description: The sixth devlog for Wild Shift, a GitHub Game Off 2026 entry, recounts a small readability bug — the player character @ kept vanishing into the grass — and the tweaks made so the hero stands out in a screen full of monochrome ASCII glyphs.

item.title: How BeamNG.drive Brought Its Soft-Body Physics to PS5
item.description: The BeamNG team shares how it kept the game's soft-body physics intact on PS5, and how it optimized memory and performance for the console.

item.title: Mesh Engine for Unity - spatial partitioning for large CAD imports
item.description: This Unity asset uses spatial partitioning to handle large CAD imports smoothly, born from the author's digital twin work.

item.title: How I built unofficial native 64-bit Linux/ARM64 SDL2 engines for a few classic PC games
item.description: A technical note on writing unofficial native 64-bit Linux and ARM64 SDL2 engines so a few classic PC games can run cleanly without Wine or an old 32-bit stack.

item.title: Spine vs Exode: Skeletal Animation for Games vs Skeletal Animation for Interfaces
item.description: Spine has been the default 2D skeletal animation tool in games for over a decade, while Exode added bones, IK and weight painting in the past year; their feature lists look alike on paper, but they target different artifacts, and picking the wrong one can cost months — this piece draws the practical line between them.
